capture.final_message:
Use the Radon–Nikodym density representation throughout.

First, apply the “RN derivative of a density” theorem to  
\(f=d\nu/d\mu\): the measure \(\mu.withDensity\,f\) has RN derivative \(f\) with respect to \(\mu\), giving the first almost-everywhere equality. Sigma-finiteness supplies the required Radon–Nikodym hypotheses.

For the equivalence, prove both universally quantified statements independently:

- The left side is the standard reconstruction formula
  \[
  \nu.withDensity\,(d\mu/d\nu)=\mu
  \]
  when \(\mu\ll\nu\), using the available Lebesgue decomposition.

- For the right side, first reconstruct
  \(\nu_i=\mu.withDensity\,f_i\), where \(f_i=d\nu_i/d\mu\). Expand measure convolution, use Tonelli/Fubini, and use left invariance of \(\mu\) to change variables. This identifies
  \[
  \nu_1*\nu_2=\mu.withDensity\,(f_1*_{\mu}f_2),
  \]
  after which uniqueness of Radon–Nikodym derivatives gives the asserted almost-everywhere equality.

Since both propositions are established outright, assemble the `Iff` by constant implications rather than trying to specialize the convolution statement to recover the general reconstruction theorem.
